articles.title: Harvard Researchers Develop New Metasurface Design with Intentionally Designed Antireflective Coating
articles.summary: Researchers at Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences have made a significant breakthrough in metasurface design by incorporating an intentionally designed antireflective coating into their devices.
articles.content: Researchers at Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences have made a significant breakthrough in metasurface design by incorporating an intentionally designed antireflective coating into their devices. This innovation could pave the way for wider adoption of metasurfaces in practical applications. The team, led by Federico Capasso, has been working on metasurfaces for some time, and these ultrathin optical devices are already being used to replace plastic lenses in smartphones. A major advantage of metalens technology is its ability to precisely control light, making it ideal for depth-sensing systems. A key challenge in developing more efficient metasurfaces has been the issue of unwanted reflections. Some of the incoming light is redirected away from its intended path, reducing the device's efficiency. To address this problem, Capasso and his team have engineered a new two-layer design that incorporates nanoscale pillars to minimize reflection. The researchers' solution involves stacking two layers of freestanding nanostructures on top of each other. This bilayer titanium dioxide metasurface is the result of years of work by the Capasso group, who are now refining their technology to make it even more effective. Their latest innovation has been published in Nature Nanotechnology and represents a critical step forward for metasurface development. The potential applications for this technology are vast, from smartphones to medical devices, and could have a significant impact on various industries. The technology developed by researchers has far-reaching potential, but first it needs to overcome a major challenge: unwanted reflections in devices. A metasurface may appear uniform at first glance, but its nanoscale pillars vary in size and shape across the surface, each with its own unique effect on light as it passes through. This variation makes it difficult to apply a conventional thin-film antireflection coating that could improve overall reflection but wouldn't be optimized for every local geometry. Co-first author Davide Cassara explained that the researchers encountered this problem while working on their experiments, and they needed a solution that would provide point-by-point antireflection properties to the entire structure. To address this issue, they created a second titanium dioxide layer co-engineered with the first layer, which provides tailored antireflection capabilities. The upper pillar in the bilayer design is specifically tailored to the geometry beneath it, allowing for local control over reflection. This design freedom enables researchers to explore new possibilities in optical functionalities that aren't possible with a single layer. The second layer not only guards against unwanted reflections but also adds numerous degrees of design flexibility for devices. For instance, differently shaped and oriented layers can produce different polarization responses or directions of reflected light, while additional layers could improve efficiency and support more complex functions such as achromatic lenses. The innovative technology has far-reaching implications for various industries, including augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR), where multilayer metalenses could play a crucial role in advancing these cutting-edge systems. Researchers believe that this method can be adapted to other materials beyond glass, such as silicon, if suitable fabrication processes become widely available. This would enable the creation of optical devices with unique properties, paving the way for new applications in fields like spectroscopy and biological imaging. The research is a testament to the value of long-term collaborations between academia and industry, where experts from both sectors come together to push the boundaries of innovation. By combining materials science and engineering expertise, researchers can create real-world products that have a significant impact on various industries. This project demonstrates the potential for driving advancements in optical lens technology across multiple industries, as Paulo Dainese, senior principal scientist at Corning, noted. His statement highlights the importance of collaboration between industry leaders and academic institutions in shaping the future of technological development. The innovative design of a two-layer flat lens has been successfully demonstrated by researchers using nanoscale pillars to minimize unwanted reflections. This pioneering technology is poised to revolutionize various fields such as optics and photonics, where conventional lenses often suffer from distortion and aberration due to their curved shape. A flat lens that can focus light without any curvature would be a game-changer, one expert notes. The breakthrough achievement represents a significant step forward in the development of more efficient and versatile optical systems. articles.title: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin poised to announce presidential candidacy
articles.summary: Dominique de Villepin is set to formally launch his presidential campaign this Friday, taking on a crowded field of candidates vying for the presidency in 2027.
articles.content: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin is poised to announce his candidacy for the country's highest office, with plans to formally launch his presidential campaign this Friday. De Villepin's decision has been met with both interest and skepticism, as he prepares to take on a crowded field of candidates vying for the presidency in 2027. De Villepin's team has scheduled a press conference at Paris's Maison de l'Amerique Latine, a cultural center established by General Charles de Gaulle in the aftermath of World War II. The event is expected to draw significant attention, as De Villepin seeks to differentiate himself from other contenders and establish his vision for France's future. De Villepin has been vocal about his opposition to certain policies, including Israel's Gaza campaign, which has resonated with younger voters. However, it remains to be seen whether this stance will translate into electoral success for the former prime minister. The press conference is set to take place at 11am on Friday, and De Villepin's team has framed the event as an opportunity for him to present himself as a unifying force in French politics. De Villepin's campaign is built on his criticism of three main forces in French politics: the far-right National Rally, which currently leads the polls; France Unbowed, a left-wing party that came second in the last election; and what he terms the "Macronist centre. He views these groups as responsible for France's decline. The former prime minister is set to call on voters not to give up hope for change in the 2027 presidential election. Instead of accepting the status quo, he wants to present himself as a symbol of renewal. De Villepin is expected to urge people to resist what he sees as a predetermined outcome. Preparations for his candidacy have been underway for over two years. During this time, De Villepin has been actively building his public profile through various means. He has created his own political party, Humanist France", written a book, and expanded his online presence on social media platforms. De Villepin's team claims to have secured commitments from 300 mayors across the country in support of his candidacy. However, it remains unclear whether this will be sufficient for him to meet the requirement of gathering at least 500 signatures from mayors needed to run for office. The obstacle that prevented Dominique de Villepin from running for president in 2012 was his inability to gather enough signatures from mayors to meet the requirement. This setback has not deterred De Villepin's ambitions, however, and he is now poised to announce his candidacy. De Villepin's long-standing presence on France's political scene, dating back to the 1980s when he served as a key strategist for Jacques Chirac, has earned him respect from both sides of the aisle. His insightful analysis of international affairs has garnered a significant following among those who would not have normally considered supporting a right-wing politician. Despite his low polling numbers, currently ranging between one to three percent, De Villepin's opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip has helped him tap into a younger, more left-leaning electorate that might otherwise dismiss him. The practice of creating intricate mathematical problems on wooden tablets, known as sangaku, was once widespread but is now largely forgotten. The Edo period, spanning from 1603 to 1868, saw the creation of thousands of these painted tablets, but only about 900 remain today. To preserve this cultural heritage, a team led by Antonia Karaisl at Waseda University in Tokyo has digitized many of them and made them available online through the Sangaku Archive. The archive is a valuable resource for anyone interested in mathematics and Japanese culture. "Sangaku have sort of fallen off the radar of public knowledge in Japan," says Karaisl, who hopes that documenting these tablets will help raise their profile both within and outside the country. These mathematical artworks are not simply decorative; they often feature complex problems involving geometry and algebra. Their beauty and precision make them a fascinating glimpse into the mathematical thinking of the past. The intricate geometry of sangaku tablets has long fascinated mathematicians and historians alike. A classic example is found in Konnoh Hachimangu Shrine in Tokyo, where a tablet presents a series of interconnected circles. The central white circle is partially surrounded by another circle, while three smaller red circles with diameters of 4 units are nestled inside the yellow circle with a diameter of 5 units. A black line at the bottom of the diagram prompts the viewer to calculate its length, which is given as 16 units along with an elementary geometric method for arriving at that solution. However, the tablet does not provide a proof for why this method is correct. This was typical of sangaku's purpose - to pose a challenge rather than simply convey mathematical knowledge. Karaisl notes that sangaku were designed to advertise the mathematical skills available in private schools, where such knowledge was often restricted. By presenting problems and solutions without explanation, these tablets served as a kind of intellectual teaser, inviting viewers to ponder and explore the underlying mathematics for themselves. The absence of explicit proof on sangaku tablets was not merely an oversight but rather a deliberate choice, meant to encourage independent thinking and problem-solving skills in those who encountered them. This approach reflects the cultural context in which these mathematical puzzles were created, where knowledge was often guarded closely by private institutions seeking to maintain their reputation for excellence. The construction of sangaku, Japan's mathematical puzzle tablets, served more than one purpose according to some experts. These puzzles were not just created for public display; individuals also used them as a means of personal commemoration or simply for the joy of creating something new. A researcher on the Sangaku Archive project notes that people may have built these puzzles for reasons beyond their intended function as mathematical challenges, echoing the sentiment that humans often seek to leave a lasting legacy. The idea is not unlike modern-day social media platforms where individuals share their achievements and creations with others. When examining the sangaku, one can't help but think of video games that incorporate puzzles as part of the gameplay experience. A game like The Witness comes to mind, which takes place on an island filled with puzzles that involve drawing lines on a grid in order to solve them. While this may sound straightforward, the sense of discovery and interaction between the player and the game developer is what makes it engaging. The process of building the Sangaku Archive was also a journey of discovery for its creator. A book published in 1998 provided the locations of known sangaku, but actually accessing these sites proved to be a more laborious task. Visiting over 400 sangaku locations has become a daunting task for Karaisl, who often finds herself at small rural shrines that are accessible only by foot or bike. In one instance, she cycled to a remote temple in the mountains, expecting to find the sangaku on display, but instead found herself stuck on the wrong side of a river. The Japanese approach to mathematics was distinct from its Western counterpart, with an emphasis on experimental calculations rather than deduction, according to Tsukane Ogawa at Yokkaichi University. This unique methodology allowed Japanese mathematicians to develop many results independently, sometimes even before their European counterparts, such as the development of calculus by Newton and Leibniz in the 17th century. Many sangaku display a particular way of doing mathematics that is unfamiliar to Western-trained eyes. This was partly due to Japan's isolationist outlook towards Europe during the Edo period. Tsukane Ogawa at Yokkaichi University notes that Japanese mathematicians focused on experimental calculations, rather than deduction, and were uninterested in Euclid's Elements when it arrived in Japan via a Chinese translation. The unique approach of Japanese mathematicians in the past is characterized by their focus on experimental calculations rather than deductive reasoning. This method is exemplified by sangaku, a series of mathematical problems presented visually on stone or wooden tablets for public display. Karaisl and her team are continuing to work with the archive, aiming to share its contents with a wider audience beyond academia. The beauty of these historical artifacts lies not only in their aesthetic appeal but also in their representation of a culture that valued mathematics as a form of public art. articles.title: El Niño Threatens Global Banana Supplies
articles.summary: A severe El Niño event could lead to a 65% reduction in banana harvests due to drought or excessive rain, prompting growers to seek higher prices from wholesalers.
articles.content: Bananas have been a staple at supermarkets, priced affordably to entice customers. However, their relatively low cost is set to rise due to the looming threat of an intense El Niño event, which could wreak havoc on banana crops thousands of miles away. El Niño's impact on banana yields can be dramatic, with less rainfall hindering growth and resulting in potential harvest losses of up to 65%. Conversely, excessive rain can lead to waterlogged soil, fostering the spread of fungal and bacterial diseases that further reduce yields. Growers are now seeking higher prices from wholesalers for their crop, a move that may challenge the status quo at grocery stores where bananas have long been considered a loss leader. This shift is attributed in part to climate-driven productivity losses and increased costs. The industry's response to El Niño includes Costa Rica's National Banana Corporation urging an almost 10% hike in the minimum export price of bananas for next year, citing productivity losses and stronger currency as key factors. Fairtrade International has also approved a 5.6% increase in its average minimum prices for banana growers, effective from January. The El Niño event is expected to be particularly severe, with a 60% chance that it will surpass previous occurrences dating back to 1950. Growers are bracing themselves for the worst as they request higher prices from wholesalers in response to the looming threat. Heavy rainfall in Ecuador has caused 851 floods between August 29 and November 13, with banana-growing provinces Guayas, Los Ríos, and El Oro among those severely affected. The country's top banana exporter is now on high alert for El Niño, having issued a red alert due to the extreme weather conditions. Climate stress in Ecuador is at four times its historical level for this time of year, making it difficult for banana crops to thrive. Banana-growing regions are not only struggling with excessive rainfall but also scorching heat, which is detrimental to crop yields. For instance, bananas grown in the Philippines are being affected by high temperatures, while those in Ecuador and Costa Rica are facing waterlogged conditions. The consequences of these extreme weather events will be felt in the global banana market. According to a report shared with Fortune, growers are bracing themselves for potential losses. As import costs rise due to the Iran war's impact on diesel and fertilizer prices, the US is already seeing an increase in banana imports by volume (3% higher) and value (12% higher) compared to the same period last year. Grocery stores have been absorbing the costs of higher banana imports, keeping prices low for shoppers despite rising expenses. This strategy is not unique to the current situation, as bananas are often treated as loss leaders to attract customers and increase foot traffic in stores. By keeping retail margins extremely low, grocery stores pass the financial burden directly down to growers. However, experts warn that this may change with the strongest El Niño on record putting pressure on global supply chains. Higher import costs due to diesel and fertilizer price increases will eventually be passed on to consumers, although it's uncertain when exactly this will happen. The wholesale crisis is already underway, but retailers are hesitant to raise prices in the short term. As the situation unfolds, shoppers can expect price hikes to become a reality in the long term, despite current efforts by grocery stores to maintain low prices. Growers and suppliers will ultimately bear the brunt of higher costs, while consumers may face increased prices on store shelves when retailers decide it's time to pass on the increases. The outcome is uncertain, but one thing is clear: the impact of El Niño will be felt across the entire supply chain. articles.title: BepiColombo Spacecraft Set to Enter Mercury's Orbit on November 21st
articles.summary: The BepiColombo spacecraft is set to enter Mercury's orbit on November 21st after an eight-year journey, marking a major milestone in the mission.
articles.content: The BepiColombo spacecraft is set to enter Mercury's orbit on November 21st, marking a major milestone in its eight-year journey. As part of this mission, BepiColombo will conduct an extensive examination of the planet's geological features, its thin atmosphere, and its magnetic field over the course of the next year. This research aims to shed light on Mercury's formation and evolution throughout history. By studying these aspects, scientists hope to gain a deeper understanding of the planet's complex processes. BepiColombo is a joint venture between the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), which was launched in October 2018. Due to Mercury's proximity to the sun, reaching the planet requires a precise trajectory that avoids overshooting its orbit and falling into the solar body. To achieve this, the spacecraft took a circuitous route, utilizing the gravity of Venus and Mercury themselves on multiple occasions to make subtle adjustments to its path. The dual-orbiting design of the BepiColombo spacecraft allows for a unique approach to studying Mercury's environment and its interactions with the solar wind. While the two orbiters are distinct entities, they share a common objective: to gather insights into the planet's mysterious exosphere and magnetic field. The Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) is significantly larger than its counterpart, the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The MPO's extensive suite of instruments focuses on surveying Mercury's surface composition, terrain, and atmospheric properties using a range of spectrometers and a laser altimeter. This information will be crucial in understanding the planet's geological history and evolution over time. In contrast, MMO's more distant orbit allows it to study the broader magnetic field and atmosphere surrounding Mercury, as well as the solar wind that significantly impacts this region close to the sun. The prolonged orbit of MMO around Mercury is actually an advantage in studying the planet's magnetic field and atmosphere, as well as the effects of the solar wind on this region near the sun. Despite its challenges, the mission could be extended for another year if necessary, but eventually the limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it difficult to continue. Mercury's enigmatic magnetic field is particularly puzzling because it originates at a height of 400 kilometres above the planet's centre, where one would expect it to have dissipated long ago. The planet's atmosphere must be constantly replenished with material from the surface, but scientists are still unsure about the exact process by which this occurs. Mercury's massive iron core is another mystery that BepiColombo will help to unravel, as its size and proportion relative to other planets in the solar system pose significant questions about the planet's formation and evolution. articles.title: Youth Protests Erupt Across Europe This Weekend
articles.summary: Protesters will take to the streets across several European nations as part of a larger movement against soaring housing costs and deteriorating learning conditions.
articles.content: Youth protests are set to erupt across Europe this weekend, with over 25 countries joining forces to voice their discontent with soaring housing costs and deteriorating learning conditions. The coordinated demonstrations aim to increase pressure on governments and demonstrate cross-border solidarity among protesters. Protesters will take to the streets in several European nations, including France, Britain, Belgium, Spain, Italy, Portugal, and Greece, as part of a larger movement that has already brought hundreds of thousands onto the streets. Local grievances have fueled the protests, but shared concerns about housing costs, learning conditions, stagnant pay, and increased military spending unite the movements. The demonstrations come at a critical time for Europe, with Russia's invasion of Ukraine approaching its fifth year and several key elections scheduled in Spain, France, Italy, and Greece. The show of force aims to send a clear message to governments that protesters will not be ignored or silenced. Unions and activists are pushing the envelope by holding simultaneous rallies on Friday and over the weekend, raising the stakes for governments to address the growing concerns of their citizens. Youth-led movements are planning simultaneous protests across 25 countries as part of a growing wave of demonstrations against rising living costs. Zennor Tyndale-Biscoe, a 17-year-old student from southwest England, is among the organisers who believe their voices will have a significant impact on policymakers. According to Tyndale-Biscoe, this event provides an opportunity for young people to express their need for systemic and immediate change, which is essential for their futures. The youth-led coalition's demands are far-reaching and include radical transformations of the current system, an end to militarisation, and a fight against social injustice. The group has called on young people to take action and protest against policies that prioritise war over their future well-being. France's Yellow Vests movement is also involved in the planning process, bringing with it experience from its successful street protests in 2018 and 2019, which put pressure on President Emmanuel Macron's government. The fear of being drafted into military service is driving many young Germans to take part in the upcoming cost of living protests. Hannes Kramer, a student protester, expressed his discontent by highlighting the stark contrast between the vast sums being allocated to the military and infrastructure, and the dismantling of social welfare services. He pointed out that while money seems to be no object when it comes to funding the armed forces, essential public programs are being stripped away. The scale of the protests remains uncertain, but organizers anticipate hundreds of demonstrations and strikes in countries like Portugal, Croatia, and Switzerland. The scope of the mobilization is difficult to predict, but one thing is clear: young people across Europe are growing increasingly frustrated with their economic circumstances. In France, the timing of the protests coincides with a significant anniversary, eight years since the Yellow Vest movement first emerged as a response to rising fuel taxes. Over time, its focus shifted from fuel prices to broader concerns about living costs and government policies. The demonstrations in Italy will coincide with a general strike that is expected to disrupt transport, schools, and hospitals, with the CGIL trade union labeling it "the country's call for change". Youthful discontent has been spreading rapidly across Europe, with protests erupting in 25 countries as young people demand change from their governments. Inspired by French students who took to blocking their high schools in mid-September to push for better learning conditions, these mass demonstrations are now a hallmark of the region's growing unrest. The school movement in France quickly snowballed into a nationwide campaign against soaring prices and inadequate public services, with some protesters even taking aim at police brutality. In several countries, including Belgium, Italy, and Spain, young people have taken to social media to share their experiences using the hashtag "blocus", which originated from the French word for blockade. This online movement has been accompanied by on-the-ground protests, where thousands have spoken out against the harsh effects of tear gas and even suffered severe injuries at the hands of police. articles.title: Lauren Boebert's Congressional Office Being Packed Up After Midterm Election Loss
articles.summary: Rep. Lauren Boebert has been reflecting on her loss in the midterm elections, which saw Democrats take control of Congress.
articles.content: Rep. Lauren Boebert's congressional office is being packed up after her loss in the midterm elections. The Colorado Republican has been reflecting on the outcome of the election, which saw Democrats take control of Congress and send a clear message to the GOP. Boebert recently spoke via Zoom from a U-Haul van parked outside one of her properties, looking back on her time as a prominent figure in the MAGA movement. She acknowledged that voters did not return her to Washington, D.C., where she had been representing her district for just two years. In her first interview since her loss, Boebert touched on the possible reasons behind her defeat. The election outcome could be seen as a referendum on President Trump's leadership and policies, according to Boebert. She also suggested that it might reflect poorly on Congress or the Republican Party as a whole, although she declined to directly blame any one aspect of the party's platform. Boebert emphasized that she is not holding anything against President Trump personally, but acknowledged that certain actions taken by him may have had a negative impact on her voters. The shift in Lauren Boebert's stance on the "Make America Great Again movement is evident in her recent actions and statements. As one of its most vocal supporters, she made headlines with her right-wing views from 2020 onwards, but now appears less inclined to define herself by such labels. On Fox News four years ago, Boebert described herself as ultra MAGA, a label that no longer seems fitting for her current position. Her words on the matter are clear: When Jesus comes back and I’m raptured up, like all these labels are just going to fly off anyway. This statement reflects her desire to move beyond such definitions. Boebert maintains that she hasn't undergone significant changes in six years, apart from a few more gray hairs and possibly some personal growth. However, she acknowledges the importance of bipartisanship, an area where she claims to have made progress. Despite this supposed personal growth, Boebert's actions continue to raise eyebrows. In 2023, she was caught vaping at a performance of Beetlejuice in Denver and escorted out of the theater. The incident was replayed in campaign ads against her that she partly credits for her loss. Boebert's decision not to dwell on past mistakes is evident as she jokingly said she wouldn't have done anything differently, except perhaps not attending the theater. Her willingness to move forward suggests a desire to distance herself from some of the controversies surrounding her time in office. Boebert's willingness to move forward suggests a desire to distance herself from some of the controversies surrounding her time in office. She has acknowledged past mistakes and apologized for them, but still feels that they are being unfairly dredged up. Some voters may have been more concerned with putting an end to the drama than with the truth of these allegations. They may have said, I don't care if any of this is true or not, I'm tired of the drama. Boebert's former district in western Colorado was a key part of her past electoral efforts, where she had previously apologized for her mistakes up and down the region. She later moved to a more conservative House seat covering the state's Great Plains, winning there in 2024 before losing two years later. Her opponent in that election raised significantly more campaign funds than Boebert did. Boebert has been open about her reluctance to raise large sums of money for her campaigns, saying I didn't raise millions of dollars and I kinda refused to." Colorado voters, she believes, know her well enough to make their own decisions. If they chose to vote against her, then that may be seen as a reflection on her performance in office. Boebert has occasionally broken with Trump's views, particularly on issues like the war in Iran and the handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files. However, she has not sought to place blame for her defeat or other GOP losses squarely at Trump's feet. As Lauren Boebert reflects on her recent electoral loss, she attributes it not just to individual factors but to broader issues affecting the Republican Party as a whole. High gas prices, internal party divisions, and unmet campaign promises are among the key reasons she cites for her defeat. These challenges, according to Boebert, hindered the party's ability to implement solutions that could have made a difference. Boebert views her loss not as an end in itself but rather as a stepping stone towards future opportunities. While she doesn't specify what these prospects might entail, her tone suggests a desire for new challenges and experiences. In contrast to some of her colleagues who may be tempted by lucrative post-congressional careers, Boebert has made it clear that she intends to pursue financial success outside the realm of politics. As she sets off on this new path, Boebert's parting shot is one of optimism and determination, leaving behind the nation's capital and its associated burdens. articles.title: Kohzo Tashima to Remain in FIFA Presidential Race
articles.summary: Japanese contender Kohzo Tashima announced he will stay in the running for FIFA presidency despite opposition from the Asian Football Confederation.
articles.content: Kohzo Tashima, a Japanese contender for the FIFA presidency, has announced he will remain in the running to replace Gianni Infantino as head of world soccer's governing body. Tashima made his intentions clear at a news conference held just outside Tokyo on Friday, citing his desire to bring about change within FIFA. He did not elaborate on what specific reforms he plans to implement. The news conference was Tashima's first since he initially announced his candidacy on November 5. In a possible sign of strategy, Tashima has expressed interest in collaborating with French candidate Philippe Diallo, who is also vying for the top spot at FIFA. Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, declared his candidacy this week and shares some moral or ethical positions with Tashima, according to the Japanese contender. Tashima's decision to stay in the running comes despite opposition from a powerful bloc: the 47-member Asian Football Confederation has pledged its support for Infantino. The AFC is headed by Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa of Bahrain, who was instrumental in securing that endorsement last month in Tokyo. Tashima's campaign against Infantino is gaining momentum as the election date approaches. He believes that the lack of attention drawn to his candidacy by some media outlets is actually a testament to his unassuming approach. According to Tashima, it's not about him being in the spotlight, but rather about giving the players the attention they deserve. His focus on fairness and integrity has resonated with many who are critical of Infantino's leadership. Infantino, seeking his fourth term, faces growing opposition as concerns over his presidency continue to mount. The election is set for March 18, a date that marks a crucial turning point in FIFA's future direction. Tashima has repeatedly emphasized the need for change and reform within FIFA, highlighting the importance of integrity and high moral standards. He believes that these values are essential for the organization's continued credibility and success. FIFA's current president, Gianni Infantino, has received criticism from Tashima, who believes that Infantino's actions have raised questions about his integrity. Infantino's annual income is substantial, nearing $6 million at current exchange rates, which has sparked debate over the distribution of World Cup revenue. According to FIFA rules, this income belongs to the organization as a whole, not just the president. The election process for FIFA's top position is complex, with different requirements depending on the number of candidates running. In a two-candidate race, Infantino would need support from 106 out of 211 member federations to secure re-election.
